document.title: Make the skill fetch sources itself and run on any forge
document.summary: The skill's step-2 call fetches the request body and review comments through the forge CLI the remote URL names, the Refresh copy uses Node in place of curl and jq, and the PR-comment pin rule maps any forge's fields. The `.agents` copy is regenerated.
document.why: The skill runs installed on users' machines, with no Comprehende checkout and on any git forge, so [its text must not assume this repo's eval layout or GitHub](source:s1).

sources.label: Claude Code session · Oct 25
sources.gist: Make the skill independent of this repo's setup and of any git forge. The agent fetches the sources; the user names only the change.

sources.label: Make the skill fetch sources itself and run on any forge
sources.gist: The agent reads the request and comments through the forge CLI picked from the remote URL. Refresh uses Node instead of curl and jq.

lookFor: Subtle. The eval producer prompt in `scripts/eval/producer.ts` still tells the agent that sources are files on disk. That prompt overrides the forge fetch during an eval run, so eval cases keep working without a change to this diff.

groups.title: Agent fetches the sources
groups.why: [The user names only the change; the agent must get the request body and comments itself](source:s1), on whatever forge the repository uses.
groups.summary: The step-2 block in `SKILL.md` replaces the `<sourcesDir>` loop with two placeholder fetch lines piped through `head -c 10000`, the paragraph below it says the remote URL names the forge CLI, and `powershell.md` mirrors the two fetches with `Out-String`.
lookFor: The two fetch lines are placeholders inside a code block. The agent substitutes the forge CLI command, so a harness without a forge CLI or MCP has no source other than the commit log.

groups.title: Refresh copy uses Node
groups.why: [The compatibility line promises Node, git, and a shell](source:s2); the POSIX Refresh block also needed `jq`.
groups.summary: The POSIX Refresh copy in `SKILL.md` runs the same Node one-liner `powershell.md` already used, and `powershell.md` drops the sentence that contrasted it with curl and jq.

groups.title: Pin fields on any forge
groups.why: [The pin rule must work on any forge](source:s1); GitHub's field names were the only mapping given.
groups.summary: The PR-comments bullet in `SKILL.md` gains one sentence that asks the agent to map each forge's own fields onto `side`, `line`, open, and outdated, and keeps the GitHub names as the example.

groups.title: Regenerated .agents copy
groups.why: `pnpm sync:skill` copies `skills-next/comprehende` into `.agents/skills/comprehende`, and the two must match.
groups.summary: Both files under `.agents/skills/comprehende` repeat the `skills-next` hunks byte for byte, so the reader can skip them.

commits.subject: Make the skill fetch sources itself and run on any forge
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
The agent reads the request body and review comments through the forge CLI it picks from the remote URL, instead of a sources directory the user names. The Refresh copy uses Node instead of curl and jq, which the compatibility line never promised.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
